$comment: The full ML catalogue: which algorithm serves which product feature. Note the code comment says 15; PIPELINE actually lists 16 distinct algorithms.

meta.title: The ML Brain - 16 algorithms behind 8 features

image_prompt: Create a clean capability map diagram, flat modern style, 16:9. Three vertical columns joined by arrows. LEFT COLUMN headed 'Learning family' with four grouped labels: 'Supervised - regression', 'Supervised - classification', 'Unsupervised', 'Probabilistic / sequence'. MIDDLE COLUMN headed 'Algorithm' listing sixteen small rounded pills: Linear Regression, Random Forest, Neural Network, KNN, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, AdaBoost, SVM, Naive Bayes, K-Means, Gaussian Mixture (EM), Hierarchical Clustering, PCA, Fisher Discriminant (LDA), Hidden Markov Model, Bayesian Network. RIGHT COLUMN headed 'Product feature' with eight boxes: 'ETA prediction', 'Fare estimation', 'Cancellation risk', 'Fraud check', 'Surge zones', 'Rider segments', 'Driver shift', 'Cancellation causes'. Draw arrows from each algorithm pill to the feature it serves, letting several arrows converge on the same feature to show ensembling. Use a distinct purple tint for the whole middle column. Keep every label horizontal and legible - this diagram is mostly text, so prioritise typography and spacing over decoration.

style.look: educational diagram, flat modern, generous whitespace, teaching-poster clarity
principles: Show the mechanism, not just the name. A reader should finish understanding WHY it works.
Prefer one worked example with real numbers over an abstract restatement.
Use colour to encode state (frontier / visited / chosen), never for decoration.
Keep formulas large and readable; put them in their own panel, not inside a node.

features.combination: three regressors averaged into an ensemble minute figure
Random Forest is the headline price; KNN is the sanity check

features.purpose: reduce rider behaviour to a plottable 2-D space and separate the classes
infer the hidden state sequence idle / en-route / on-trip from observations
reason about which factors cause cancellations, not merely which correlate

plus_non_ml.name: A* search
plus_non_ml.role: shortest path for drive and walk routing - graph search, not learning

spec.orchestration: POST /quote is the one call that chains three of these together: ETA -> fare (which needs the ETA) -> cancellation risk, returning all of it plus an estimated wait in a single response.
annotations: Accuracy note: app.py and the README both say '15 ML algorithms', but the PIPELINE map in models.py lists 16 distinct names (Random Forest appears in two features). The 16 above is what the code actually registers.
Every model trains on synthetic data at container boot, which takes about 20 seconds - that is why the deploy health check allows a 60 second budget.
Per-feature detail already exists in Diagram/algorithms/*.json; this map is the index over them.
